title: Electronics Fundamentals Module 2: DC Circuits, Series/Parallel & Kirchhoff's Laws
overview: Covers Ohm's Law, Watt's Law, Series vs. Parallel rules, KVL, and KCL for troubleshooting DC breadboard circuits.
art: • Current (I) is SAME everywhere            • Voltage (V) is SAME on branches
KIRCHHOFF'S VOLTAGE LAW (KVL) (?3)          KIRCHHOFF'S CURRENT LAW (KCL) (?4)
(All voltage drops equal source!)            (Current in = Current out!) └─► 40mA

1.label: Series Circuit Rules & Voltage Drops
1.what: Components connected end-to-end along a single path. Current has nowhere else to go, so amperage stays identical through every resistor.
1.exam_facts: R_total = R1 + R2 + R3... | I_total = I1 = I2 | V_total = V1 + V2. Bigger resistors drop more voltage (V = I × R).
1.troubleshoot: If one component opens (burns out) in a series circuit, current drops to 0A everywhere, and you will measure the FULL source voltage across the broken/open component.

2.label: Parallel Circuit Rules & Branch Resistance
2.what: Components connected across the same two voltage rails. Every branch gets full source voltage, while total current splits across paths.
2.exam_facts: V_total = V1 = V2 | I_total = I1 + I2 | 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2. Total resistance in parallel is ALWAYS smaller than the smallest individual resistor!
2.troubleshoot: If one branch opens in parallel, the other branches keep working normally, but total circuit current (I_total) decreases.

3.label: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) & Watt's Law
3.what: The sum of all voltage rises (sources) and voltage drops (loads) around any closed loop equals zero.
3.exam_facts: Watt's Law for Power: P = I × V (also P = I²R and P = V²/R). Standard breadboard resistors are rated for 1/4 Watt (0.25W)—exceeding this makes them smoke!
3.troubleshoot: If your voltage drops don't add up to your power supply voltage on a breadboard, check for a bad jumper wire or loose ground rail.

4.label: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL)
4.what: Total current entering a junction (node) must equal the total current leaving that node—electrons don't vanish or pile up.
4.exam_facts: I_entering = I_leaving. Used to analyze combination (series-parallel) circuits and current dividers.
4.troubleshoot: A sudden spike in total current draw on your bench power supply usually means a short circuit (a component failed closed or a wire bridged to ground).
